dataset.orders.protocol: Generated population size. Valmo publishes no proprietary data, so the order book is a calibrated simulation; marginals are verified against the case brief (see models/dataset_summary.json:calibration_vs_case_brief).

dataset.pincodes.protocol: Distinct India Post pincodes drawn from the bharataddress reference table.

dataset.districts.protocol: Distinct districts spanned by the generated order book.

dataset.blended_rto.protocol: Realised rate in the SIMULATED population, against the case brief's own 15/17/22 distance table. All three bands are matched to within sampling noise (0.04pp on the blended rate against the brief's 17.0% headline), which is the rounding the brief itself licenses. The financial model uses the brief's 17.0% baseline, the conservative choice, since a higher assumed baseline inflates the savings.

dataset.cod_rto.protocol: Realised COD failure rate. Case brief Exhibit: 20.0%.

dataset.prepaid_rto.protocol: Realised prepaid failure rate. Case brief Exhibit: 5.0%.

dataset.distance_penalty.protocol: Far-drop (10km+) failure rate divided by nearby (~2km) rate, measured on 100,000 orders. The generator intercept and distance coefficient were solved numerically so this reproduces the case brief Exhibit B figure of +46.67% to within Bernoulli sampling noise.

dataset.case_penalty.protocol: Nearby 15.0% vs far 22.0% undelivered. The generated population is calibrated to reproduce exactly this ratio.

dataset.near_rto.protocol: Realised failure rate for drops within ~2 km of the LMDC.

dataset.moderate_rto.protocol: Realised failure rate for ~5 km drops.

dataset.far_rto.protocol: Realised failure rate for 10 km+ drops.

dataset.s_addr_corr.protocol: Correlation between the navigability score S_addr and delivery outcome. Negative means more navigable addresses fail less often, which is the mechanism the address-quality intervention targets.

rto.roc_auc.protocol: 80/20 stratified holdout; models fit on the 80% only. All metrics below are out-of-sample. N=20,000.

rto.pr_auc.protocol: Average precision. Beats the no-skill prevalence baseline of 0.1704 by 1.51x.

rto.cv_auc.protocol: Mean of 5 stratified folds on the training split, +/- 0.0053 standard deviation. Reported so the holdout score can be sanity-checked against training variance.

rto.brier_reduction.protocol: 3-fold isotonic calibration inside CalibratedClassifierCV cuts the Brier score from 0.2305 to 0.1352 on the 20,000-order holdout. This is the load-bearing result: the cost-sensitive thresholds downstream are only meaningful on calibrated probabilities.

rto.brier_calibrated.protocol: Calibrated Brier score on the holdout split.

rto.brier_raw.protocol: Uncalibrated Brier score on the same holdout, for contrast.

rto.precision_top10.protocol: Precision among the riskiest 10% of the 20,000-order holdout: 597 of 2,000 flagged orders genuinely failed.

rto.recall_top10.protocol: Share of all real failures captured by reviewing the riskiest 10% of orders.

rto.lift_top10.protocol: Precision multiple over random targeting (baseline precision 0.1704). This, not ROC-AUC, is what justifies a fixed operational budget.

rto.targeting_swing.protocol: Value created per 1,000 orders by applying the coupon policy at its cost-optimal threshold instead of discounting every order. Blanket discounting loses Rs.14.56 per order; targeting makes money.

uplift.auuc.protocol: Trained on a synthetic RCT (N=40,000, randomised W~Bernoulli(0.40)) aligned to Valmo order marginals. Valmo publishes no randomised trial data. Unconfoundedness holds by construction; ground-truth CATE is retained to audit estimator recovery. AUUC is the raw Qini area, per Künzel et al. (2019).

uplift.auuc_random.protocol: Mean AUUC over 200 random permutations of the same evaluation set. This is the null the model must beat.

uplift.auuc_perfect.protocol: AUUC of an oracle that ranks every true responder first. Upper bound.

uplift.auuc_norm.protocol: Normalised AUUC: (AUUC_model - AUUC_random) / (AUUC_perfect - AUUC_random). 0 is random targeting, 1 is perfect targeting.

uplift.lift_over_random.protocol: Relative AUUC improvement over random targeting.

uplift.p_value.protocol: One-sided permutation test over 200 shuffles. Permutation comparison within the synthetic treatment generator only; it cannot establish that the model beats random targeting in operations.

uplift.max_qini.protocol: Peak difference in generated outcomes at the best point on a synthetic Qini curve. It is not a count of actual rescued deliveries.

rto.xgb_roc_auc.protocol: XGBoost holdout ROC-AUC, reported so the LightGBM choice is a measured decision rather than an assertion. The two are within noise of each other; LightGBM is kept for its faster single-row serving path.

uplift.cv_norm.protocol: Mean normalised AUUC across 5 folds, 95% CI [0.1239, 0.1369]. Every fold clears the permutation null at p = 0.02.

uplift.cate_recovery.protocol: Correlation between the X-Learner CATE estimate and the ground-truth treatment effect used to generate the simulated RCT. Because the truth is known here, the estimator can be audited directly rather than trusted.

uplift.persuadable_pct.protocol: Share of a synthetic holdout where a model score clears an assumed cost threshold. This does not identify real customers who would respond or support an incentive policy.

uplift.econ_threshold.protocol: Synthetic-model threshold from a ₹35 treatment-cost assumption and the case-pack ₹120 reverse-cost input. It is not an operational decision rule or a recommendation to pay an incentive.

uplift.net_margin.protocol: Synthetic arithmetic only: case-pack reverse cost less an assumed treatment cost, conditional on generated treatment labels. It is not an observed margin per rescue.

uplift.mean_cate.protocol: Mean predicted conditional average treatment effect on the holdout.

tel.accuracy.protocol: Unsupervised fit (contamination="auto") on a 35,000-row training split. Operating threshold = 10th-percentile TRAIN score (ops capacity constraint, no labels). Scored once on the 15,000-row held-out split.

tel.faked_f1.protocol: F1 for generated anomaly labels in the synthetic held-out scenario. It does not measure fake attempts, misconduct, or real rider behavior.

tel.faked_precision.protocol: Precision against generated anomaly labels only. No real attempt has been independently adjudicated, so this is not a rider-safety estimate.

tel.genuine_precision.protocol: Agreement with generated normal/anomaly labels only. It does not show how often real riders would be incorrectly flagged.

tel.macro_f1.protocol: Macro-averaged F1 across both classes on held-out data.

tel.faked_recall_pct.protocol: Recall against generated anomaly labels only; no real attempt rate or misconduct prevalence is estimated.

tel.audit_budget.protocol: Operating point set by an ops capacity constraint, NOT by label prevalence. The model is fitted with contamination="auto" and the threshold is the 10th percentile of TRAINING anomaly scores, so no test label informs the threshold.

tel.model_size.protocol: Serialised Isolation Forest prototype size, 300 trees at max_samples=256. No rider-app integration or deployment assessment has been completed.

serving.p99.protocol: 200 sequential single-order inferences after 300 warm-up calls, measured in-process. Payloads are synthetic and timing is machine-dependent; this is not a deployment SLA. The single-order and batch paths are numerically identical by running python predict.py --parity, so the latency claim and the batch numbers cannot disagree.

serving.p50.protocol: Median of local single-order timing samples on the recorded machine; not a production SLA.

serving.parity.protocol: Maximum absolute P(RTO) difference between the single-order and batch serving paths over 500 orders. Zero means there is no train/serve skew between the fast path and the validated model; both paths delegate to a single _score_rto implementation, so this is an exact-equality check. Verified: True, risk-tier mismatches 0.

serving.throughput.protocol: Local batch-scoring throughput on generated examples; not a production capacity estimate.

econ.forward_rupees.protocol: Blended forward logistics cost per parcel across the seven Valmo nodes.

econ.reverse_rupees.protocol: Reverse freight incurred when a parcel fails to deliver.

econ.loaded_loss.protocol: Combined forward and reverse logistics cost for a failed parcel under the case inputs; the forward cost is already incurred and is not a saving from an incremental rescue. Maximum avoidable reverse cost is up to ₹120 before other costs.

econ.coupon_rupees.source: proposal scenario assumption; not supplied by the case brief
econ.coupon_rupees.protocol: Internal synthetic treatment-simulation cost only. It is not a proposed live incentive, participant preference, or case-pack input.

econ.lmdc_rupees.protocol: Last-mile delivery centre allocation, 42% of case-pack forward spend. This cost allocation is not evidence of negative margins on far drops.

fin.reverse_spend_baseline.protocol: Internal scenario only: annual reverse freight at assumed volume and the case-derived 17.0% baseline. Volume is not supplied by the brief.

fin.reverse_spend_target.protocol: Internal scenario only: annual reverse freight with assumed volume and a 12% target. Neither is supplied by the brief.

fin.parcels_saved_daily.protocol: Conditional arithmetic only: assumed 1.5M daily orders multiplied by an Internal scenario only: assumed volume multiplied by an assumed five-point RTO change; neither is a case requirement.

fin.per_10k_delivered.source: DICE case brief, Exhibit A cost split
fin.per_10k_delivered.protocol: Case-derived arithmetic per 10,000 orders; forward cost on failed orders is already incurred. An incremental rescue can avoid reverse freight only.

fin.per_10k_rto.source: DICE case brief, Exhibit A cost split
fin.per_10k_rto.protocol: Case-derived blended arithmetic per 10,000 orders; not an observed Valmo rate.

fin.loaded_loss_per_order.protocol: Combined forward-plus-reverse case cost for a failure; not the incremental savings from rescuing that order.

cascade.tier2_net.source: DICE case brief Exhibit A + our estimate
cascade.tier2_net.protocol: Retired internal scenario arithmetic only. The brief supplies the reverse-cost input but no middle-mile saving; do not present this as a verified benefit.

cascade.tier3_asp_ceiling.protocol: Retired eligibility assumption only; no case or operational source establishes this price ceiling.

data.india_post_pincodes.protocol: Bundled lookup snapshot count; source provenance and current coverage are not independently validated for this submission.

data.post_offices.protocol: Bundled lookup snapshot count; not an operational coverage or delivery claim.

data.registry_districts.protocol: Bundled lookup snapshot count; the synthetic order book uses a different generated coverage count.

data.geocoded_pincodes.protocol: Bundled lookup snapshot count; centroid completeness and geocoding accuracy are not independently validated for delivery use.

tel.trees.protocol: Isolation Forest tree count. An earlier ledger entry said 100 and understated the shipped model.

tel.max_samples.protocol: Sub-sample size per tree, which bounds memory footprint.

serving.bench_runs.protocol: Pooled benchmark sample count: 3 blocks x 2,000 runs. A tail quantile from a single block is unstable on a shared host.

serving.artifact_kb.protocol: Size of the calibrated classifier artifact in KB, measured at ledger-build time rather than typed in. The telemetry anomaly prototype is 3.18 MB.

econ.unpruned_mb.protocol: Size of an unpruned Isolation Forest, quoted only to contrast with the shipped 3.18 MB model.

sim.modelled_bps.protocol: Synthetic simulator output only. Components include assumed effects and effects induced by the data generator; this is not an estimate of Valmo impact.

sim.estimated_bps.protocol: Treatment-effect estimate recovered from randomized assignment in generated data only. It is a method rehearsal, not an estimate of real customer response or Valmo impact.

sim.breakeven_multiple.protocol: Ratio comparing a synthetic simulator output with a breakeven calculated from assumed costs. It is not evidence that the programme is value-positive.

sim.estimated_value_cr.protocol: Conditional scenario extrapolation from synthetic outcomes and assumed daily volume; not a forecast or measured saving.

sim.circular_bps.protocol: The address-quality nudge and the distance-tiered payout. Both act on coefficients we chose when writing the generator, so simulating them recovers an input rather than estimating an effect. Disclosed rather than folded into the headline.

sim.assumed_bps.protocol: Cross-docking salvage. The 17.5% salvage share is an operating parameter we chose and label, not a measurement. Phase 1 instrumentation will measure the local-SKU match rate.

sim.failures_reached.protocol: Share of generated baseline failures resolved inside the scenario; not an observed operating outcome.

meesho.cod_delivery_success.protocol: H1 FY26 marketplace-wide COD delivery-success rate reported in the prospectus. This is not Valmo-specific and is not converted to an RTO rate; the model continues to use the case-pack inputs.

meesho.prepaid_delivery_success.protocol: H1 FY26 marketplace-wide prepaid delivery-success rate reported in the prospectus. Not Valmo-specific; no RTO complement is inferred.

meesho.cod_share_fall_pp.protocol: Meesho's reported marketplace COD share of shipped orders fell from 88.71% in FY22 to 72.00% in H1 FY26. Historical context only; it does not establish that a proposed checkout intervention caused this change.

meesho.valmo_share.protocol: Valmo represented 64.52% of Meesho's shipped orders in H1 FY26. This is context about disclosed shipped-order share only; it does not establish Valmo-specific RTO or identify which orders used each network.

meesho.aov_fy25.protocol: Meesho's FY25 average order value. This public marketplace figure has a different scope from the case-pack assumed order value; do not use it to infer this proposal’s customer response or margin impact.

meesho.rto_assurance_programme.protocol: This product claim requires independent source and scope verification before presentation; it is not a supported point in the core deck.

rto.bayes_ceiling.protocol: ROC-AUC obtained by ranking on the TRUE conditional probability of failure, computed from the generating logit. This is the optimal possible scorer for this population and no estimator can exceed it, because it is a property of the data-generating process rather than of any fit. Disclosure: it inherits our own calibration assumptions, so it bounds what a classifier could reach on this data and is not a claim about Valmo.

rto.signal_captured.protocol: Share of the attainable signal the classifier actually captures. Answers the "0.65 AUC is weak" objection with the ceiling rather than an assertion: the residual gap is sampling noise at n=20,000, not missed structure.

rto.seed_std.protocol: Standard deviation of holdout ROC-AUC across five independent seeded splits (42, 7, 2024, 99, 1234). This is the honest error bar on the headline AUC, and shows the number is not an artefact of one lucky split.

bh.tier3_cod.protocol: Generated COD failure rate in this synthetic dataset. The tier and distance relationships reflect the simulator design; they are not Valmo findings.

bh.tier_gap.protocol: Generated tier gap in synthetic labels at the configured distance mix.

bh.addr_gap.protocol: Relative failure gap between orders carrying neither a premise nor a landmark (22.60%) and orders carrying both (14.55%) in generated labels. This is a simulator association, not evidence for the address-prompt hypothesis.

bh.first_time.protocol: Failure rate for first-time buyers against 16.4% for repeat buyers in the synthetic dataset. This pattern is generated and is not an operational measurement.

econ.per_10k_base.protocol: The paradox is worked per 10,000 orders because it divides cleanly. Any order base gives the same ratio.

econ.bps_target.protocol: Illustrative planning scenario reduction only. The case brief specifies no 500-basis-point target and the synthetic models do not estimate it.

pay.new_pay_10km.source: Proposed payout scenario: 16 base + 2.50/km beyond 5 km + 5 verified + 2 OTP
pay.new_pay_10km.protocol: Illustrative total payout on a 10 km drop against an assumed Rs 18 baseline. This arithmetic does not establish current rider pay, route cost, or rider behavior.

pay.incremental_10km.source: Derived: pay.new_pay_10km minus the Rs 18 flat fee
pay.incremental_10km.protocol: Increment over the assumed baseline. The displayed breakeven lift is conditional arithmetic before administration and other costs.

pay.net_per_rescue.source: Derived: case-pack Rs 120 reverse cost minus the assumed incremental payout
pay.net_per_rescue.protocol: Gross avoided reverse-cost arithmetic less the assumed payout; not net margin and excludes operational, administrative, and conversion costs.

eval.holdout_n.protocol: Held-out rows in the synthetic classifier evaluation.

eval.uplift_n.protocol: Arms in the simulated doorstep-rescue RCT. models/uplift_metrics.json:n is the 12,000-arm evaluation split (30% held out), not the full population.

eval.telemetry_n.protocol: Generated attempt-pattern examples in the synthetic anomaly-prototype evaluation; not real delivery attempts.

eval.telemetry_test_n.protocol: Held-out generated examples scored once; this does not validate rider monitoring or production performance.

eval.shap_n.protocol: Holdout rows on which TreeSHAP values are computed for the beeswarm plot.

econ.annual_orders_m.protocol: Orders per year: 1.5M/day x 365. Basis for the duty-cycle and cost figures.

econ.compute_hours.protocol: Illustrative compute hours using assumed order volume and local prototype timing. This is not a cloud capacity or cost estimate. Derived by calling financial_model.cost_of_ml() rather than typed, so it moves with the latency benchmark instead of drifting away from it.

method.xlearner_citation.protocol: Year of the X-Learner paper we implement. The four-stage estimator follows that formulation exactly; the AUUC evaluation convention is our own, benchmarked against a permutation null and a perfect-targeting oracle.

econ.per_1k_denominator.protocol: Unit the targeting swing is quoted per. The underlying measurement is on the 20,000-order holdout; 1,000 is the scaling convention.

econ.lmdc_share.protocol: Share of forward logistics spend concentrated at the last mile.

fin.conditional_net.protocol: Conditional scenario arithmetic: modeled gross reverse-cost savings minus the five assumed operating-cost lines. Daily volume, the full effect, and every cost line require validation; this is not EBITDA, a forecast, or realized benefit.

fin.gross_savings.protocol: Conditional gross reverse-cost arithmetic for 75,000 fewer failures/day under the assumed 1.5M orders/day and 17% to 12% RTO scenario, at the case-pack Rs 120 reverse cost. No outcome is validated.

fin.total_opex.protocol: Sum of all five operating cost lines. No cost line is omitted or netted against savings.

fin.modeled_net_to_opex.protocol: Conditional scenario net after modeled costs divided by modeled opex. This is a ratio of assumptions, not an ROI or investment return.

fin.breakeven_bps.protocol: The programme covers its own Rs 54.42 Cr cost once blended RTO falls to 16.17%. This breakeven is conditional on assumed scenario volume and modeled costs; it does not establish value-positive operations.

fin.headroom_bps.protocol: Difference between modeled-cost break-even and the assumed planning scenario reduction; not headroom against a promised target.

fin.spend_paradox.protocol: Scenario share of logistics spend associated with failed orders, counting the case-pack forward leg as incurred on a failure. Counting only the reverse leg would give 28.98%, so this framing is conditional on the case-pack forward and reverse cost definitions.

fin.ml_running_cost.protocol: Annual cost of the intelligence layer: 32 general-purpose instances under the assumed scenario volume and local prototype timing (262 calculated hours/year). This is an illustrative sizing calculation, not a vendor quote or deployment plan.

retired.93.4%: Stale telemetry accuracy from before the held-out evaluation was added. Superseded by models/telemetry_metrics.json:accuracy.
retired.96.3%: Stale telemetry genuine precision. Superseded by :genuine_precision.
retired.54.2%: Distance-penalty annotation that disagreed with the +46.7% figure in the case brief and every document. The dataset is now calibrated so the near/far ratio reproduces the brief exactly.
retired.17.3%: Unreconciled blended RTO label from before the dataset was recalibrated onto the brief's own 15/17/22 distance table. The simulated population now measures 17.07% against the brief's 17.0% headline, a 7 bps gap.
retired.22.58%: Threshold derived from the wrong decision rule (C_A/(C_A+C_F)). The whole project now uses C_A/V_reverse = 29.17%, which is also the uplift model own economic cutoff.
retired.186.81: Hand-rolled AUUC with no null distribution. Superseded by a normalised AUUC reported against a 200-permutation null with a p-value.
retired.0.869 ms: Latency figure from before the serving path was unified and profiled. Superseded by the measured benchmark, which is machine-dependent and re-derived on every run.
retired.14,327: Pre-retrain targeting swing per 1,000 orders. Superseded by models/rto_metrics.json:policy_economics.targeting_swing_rs_per_1000.
retired.14.06: Pre-retrain blanket-discount loss per order. Derived from the same metric and moved with it.
retired.4,079: Pre-retrain fast-calibrator probe count. The probe is the union of the fitted thresholds and a fixed linspace, so it changes whenever the calibrator knots change.
retired.31.7%: Pre-retrain precision at the top-10% budget.
retired.1.82: Pre-retrain lift at the top-10% budget. Kept as a bare number rather than "1.82x" so a stale value is caught in either spelling.
